judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble is a straightforward identification of parties, though the blank date ("June __, 2004") is an unfilled term that leaves the execution date indeterminate. Nothing else in the wording bears two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Schedule A and the definition of "Member" in Article I; the open date could interact with Section 2.3 (term commences on filing of Articles) but that section fixes commencement independently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital defines "Maine Act" by reference to the "Maine Lunited Liability Company" — a mangled phrase omitting the word "Act", a plain mechanical error in the very words that create a defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I separately and correctly defines "Maine Act" as 31 M.R.S.A. Chapter 13, so the recital's defective definition is cured operatively, but the double definition is a recital-versus-operative mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate consideration clause with settled meaning; nothing in it invites competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the capital contribution obligations in Section 4.1 and Schedule A; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard definitional preface; the "unless the context otherwise requires" carve-out is common and rarely litigated on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs the whole of Article I and does not contradict Section 1.2 (headings) or any operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference definition; Section 13.1 does in fact define "Additional Member".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to Section 13.1 checks out and Section 15.1 uses the term consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Control" is defined by the familiar "power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies" formula, which is inherently a question of degree but is the market-standard wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Section 12.7 (DMSA's Affiliates may compete) and the definition of Covered Person; no contradiction, though its breadth enlarges 12.7's safe harbour.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A self-referential definition of "Agreement" with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 17.10's amendment mechanism and Section 17.8's integration clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain definition of "Articles" with no vague or double-meaning language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.1 refers instead to "the Certificate", an undefined term that should read "Articles" — but the defect sits in 10.1, not here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line definition; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article VI's constitution of a three-Director Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple cross-referential definition; the cross-reference to Section 4.4 is correct.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.4 does establish Capital Accounts, and Section 15.3(ii) distributes by Capital Account balance; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition is definite; "fair market value of any property" is a valuation standard but a conventional one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1 and Schedule A set agreed values, which the definition accommodates; Schedule A's odd "$00,001.00" figure for LSB is a Schedule defect rather than one here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard Code definition with a successor-statute rule; no ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Articles VIII, XI and XIII; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition of the entity; "formed and continued" is loose but harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble and Section 2.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is a sprawling chain — "any officers, directors, Members, partners, employees, representatives or agents of a Member... or their respective Affiliates" — whose outer boundary (whose Affiliates? at what remove?) is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives Sections 12.2, 12.3, 12.4 and 12.5, and its breadth sits awkwardly with Section 17.11, which confines rights under the Agreement to Members and Managers only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line definition; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article VI; "Manager" definition expressly includes Directors, which is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard three-limb fiscal year definition; the OCR "(11)" for "(ii)" is cosmetic and clause (iii) expressly refers back to clause (ii).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with Article VIII allocations; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "such Member's interest of the profits and losses" is a garbled construction (should be "interest in"), part of a document-wide substitution of "Interest" for "share" that recurs in Sections 8.2, 13.2 and 15.3.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same slip makes phrases like "Interest Profits and Losses" in Sections 8.2(ii) and 15.3 hard to reconcile with the defined term "Interest" set here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (iii) is misnumbered "(i)", and "all policies, practices and guidelines of any governmental body" sweeps non-binding material into a defined term meant for binding law — a classic general-versus-specific scope problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Laws" is used in Sections 2.2, 2.6, 6.6 and 9.3, where treating mere "practices" as Law would materially widen restrictions on distributions and Director removal.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise statutory citation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the definition the recital garbled, curing rather than creating a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is clear on its face, but it is near-identical to the separately defined "Majority", raising a question whether the two terms differ at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5(vii) uses "a Majority" for quorum and 5.5(viii) uses "Majority Vote" for decisions, so the overlap has operative consequences; the difference (written approval included) is thin.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Majority" is defined as "a majority of the Member Votes" — a quantity, yet Section 5.5(vii) uses it as a set of persons "present in person or by proxy", a mismatch of kind.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The near-duplication with "Majority Vote" and the personified use in Sections 5.5(vii) and 5.5(xi) leave genuine doubt whether the two defined terms are interchangeable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition is clear and expressly sweeps in Directors.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.1's statement that an elected Director is designated a Manager, and with Section 12.1's liability shield.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "'Members' means two (2) or more of such Persons" is odd drafting: in a two-member LLC the plural collapses, and it is unclear whether a single remaining member could ever act as "the Members".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.2(ii) speaks of "all of the remaining Members" agreeing to continue after one member's departure, which this definition arguably makes impossible in a two-member company.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "as may be amended" leaves unstated who may amend Schedule A's vote allocation and on what authority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) lets the Secretary update Schedule A without that being an amendment to the Agreement, while Section 17.10 requires unanimity to amend — a real tension over whether votes can shift without unanimous consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula is long but mechanical; "amounts determined by the Members to be necessary to provide a reasonable reserve" is discretionary but expressly committed to the Members.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That reserve discretion is given to "the Members", whereas Section 9.2 gives the Board sole control over the timing and amount of distributions — a small allocation-of-power inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line definition; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article VII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition says Percentage Interest is "as shown on Schedule A" yet also "as determined by the unanimous written consent of the Members as adjusted from time to time" — two different governing sources in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) permits the Secretary unilaterally to update Schedule A and declares such updates not to be amendments, which cannot be squared with a unanimity requirement for adjusting Percentage Interests.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The inclusion of "Company" (a defined term meaning Dialogo, LLC) inside the list of things a "Person" includes is a mechanical slip; it plainly should read "corporation".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reading the defined "Company" into "Person" would produce absurdities in Sections 3.2 and 13.1, but the error is obvious enough to be self-correcting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining Profits and Losses simply as taxable income under §703(a), with no book/tax or §704(b) adjustments, is thin, and the citation is typographically damaged.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(iv) says the allocations are intended to comply with §704(b) and Section 4.4(ii) requires Capital Accounts under Reg. 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv), which presupposes book items this definition does not supply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear appointment definition cross-referring to Section 7.4.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1 says the Secretary is elected by the Board, matching this; Sections 2.1(iii) and 2.6 give the Secretary further tasks without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference; Section 11.1 supplies the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference is accurate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard definition with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Article VIII; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional headings clause; its own words are unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is doing real work here because the document has duplicated headings (two "Section 6.6", "ARTICLE I" used twice, "ARTICLE XV" for the miscellaneous article), so its scope as a cure for numbering errors could be contested.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (iii) is internally awkward: the Secretary "shall be required to update Schedule A" yet any such revision "shall not be deemed an amendment to this Agreement", which for a schedule that fixes Percentage Interests and Member Votes is a strong and contestable statement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It collides with Section 17.10 (unanimous written amendment) and with the "Percentage Interest" definition's unanimous-consent requirement — a genuine question whether ownership can be changed by a Secretary's pen.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite; the Board's power to adopt another trade name is clearly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.6 (fictitious name filings) and Article VI's grant of management power to the Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "shall continue in perpetuity, unless the Company is dissolved" is clear, and the second sentence separately addresses legal existence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Sections 15.2 and 15.4 (cancellation of the Articles); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain designation clause; "At any time, the Members may designate another" is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Power here is given to the Members while the parallel Section 2.5 gives the Board power over the principal place of business and Section 2.6 gives the Board qualification duties — a minor split of authority, not a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Address is specific and the Board's power to relocate is unqualified; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17.1(i) uses this address for notices to the Company, so relocation is coherent; note only that Maine formation with a Massachusetts principal office is deliberate, not inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any Jurisdiction in which the Company transacts business" is a mandatory duty of uncertain trigger, but that vagueness tracks the underlying qualification statutes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Secretary is named as the "authorized person" here while Section 2.1(iv) names Gerry Pike for the Articles; the two are sequential rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The purpose is stated first as the specific "developing Spanish language newspaper(s) and media" and then as "any lawful act or activity" — a specific object followed by an unlimited catch-all, leaving the actual scope of "the business" genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.7 forbids LSB from providing services "to the extent it relates to the business" without defining that business, so the reach of this purpose clause directly determines the reach of the exclusivity covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated powers list introduced by "including, but not limited to", the standard formulation; the OCR corruption of sub-paragraph letters ("(z)" for "(g)") is cosmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sub-paragraphs (b), (c), (k) and (j) grant powers that Section 6.8 then subjects to unanimous Board approval, but 6.8 opens "Notwithstanding any other provision", which resolves the ordering.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite sentence requiring unanimous Member approval for a merger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8's list of unanimous-Board actions does not include merger, so the two allocate different decisions to different bodies without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "has contributed or is deemed to have contributed" leaves it unstated whether any cash actually changed hands, and the operative figures are exported entirely to Schedule A.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A records LSB at "$00,001.00" for 49% and DMSA at $50,000 for 51%, a striking mismatch that makes the deemed-contribution language and Section 6.8(iii)'s DMSA reimbursement carve-out contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short, settled LLC propositions; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.3's partition waiver and Section 15.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sub-clause (ii)(a) is mechanically broken — "the respective invoices of each of DMSA" (plural formula applied to one entity), "payment form such customer", and it shifts from "client" to "customer"; (ii)(b) uses "Membership Interests", a term the Agreement never defines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Membership Interests" should be "Percentage Interests" as used in Sections 8.1 and 9.1, and the DMSA invoice priority in (ii)(a) sits awkwardly with Section 6.8(iii), which bars distributions other than to reimburse DMSA's initial capital contributions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two crisp sentences incorporating the Treasury Regulation capital-account rules; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes book capital accounting that the bare §703(a) definition of Profits and Losses does not supply, a modest incoherence with that definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "subject to such terms and conditions acceptable to the Company and each Member" makes the debt terms indeterminate, and "its Interest of the distributions" repeats the document's "Interest"/"share" slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The nonrecourse-loan sentence sits oddly beside the preceding sentence making advances a debt obligation collectible only out of Company assets; Section 15.3(i) treats Members who are creditors consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the Members have the power to exercise any and all other rights or powers of the Company" is a sweeping residual grant, immediately followed by "Except as provided herein, individually, the Members shall have no power to bind the Company" — the interaction of grant and carve-out is genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.1 vests management of the business and affairs in the Board but expressly makes itself "Subject to Section 5.1", so the two provisions each defer to the other on where ultimate authority lies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "all ordinary and necessary out-of pocket expenses incurred by the Members on behalf of the Company" is an open-ended mandatory reimbursement with no cap or approval requirement, and "a distributive Interest of Profits" is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An unconditional reimbursement right sits uneasily with Section 6.8(xiv) (unanimous Board approval for incurring any material liability) and with the Net Cash Flow definition's cross-reference back to this section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence waiver in settled terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.2 (no interest in specific Company property).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition is absolute and clear on its face; it says nothing about the consequence if a Member purports to resign anyway.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.2(ii) expressly lists "resignation" of a Member as an event causing dissolution, which presupposes a resignation this section forbids — a direct internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long procedural article; the mixed use of "a Majority" (quorum) and "Majority Vote" (decision), and clause (xi) allowing any action to be taken by written consent of "a Majority", are the only soft spots.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (xi)'s written-consent-by-Majority rule cannot easily be squared with clause (ii)'s member-specific Director election rights or with Section 17.10's requirement of unanimity for amendments, given DMSA holds 51 of 100 Member Votes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "designated a Manager by the Members for purposes of the Act" uses "the Act" where the defined term is "Maine Act"; otherwise the election and vacancy mechanics are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It opens "Subject to Section 5.1", which grants the Members residual power over anything not required to be done by the Board — leaving the boundary between Board and Member authority genuinely unsettled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed meeting mechanics; "by any other means of communication" as a catch-all after a list of specified methods is the only scope softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.3, 6.4 and 7.2 (President presides); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section carves out "except as otherwise provided in Section 6.9 of this Agreement", but the Agreement contains no Section 6.9 — a dangling cross-reference in the operative exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The intended target is plainly Section 6.8 (Actions Requiring Unanimous Approval of the Board), and the tie-break sentence sending deadlocks to the Members interacts with Section 5.5 and with DMSA's 51-vote majority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard telephonic-participation clause; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 5.5(x) for Members; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It bars committees from taking "any of the actions described in Section 6.9", a section that does not exist, and the committee empowerment clause otherwise delegates "all the powers and authority of the Board".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The intended reference is Section 6.8; as written, a committee of one Director could arguably exercise every Board power, which cannot be reconciled with 6.8's unanimity protections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The compensation power is clear; the heading is numbered "Section 6.6", the same number the next section bears, a mechanical numbering error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(x) requires unanimous Board approval for employment and other contracts with Directors and Officers, which arguably qualifies the free-standing power to fix Director compensation here.
